newsitem.title: UK: Michael Jackson proudly shows off baby son.
newsitem.headline: Michael Jackson proudly shows off baby son.

text.p: Michael Jackson on Tuesday proudly showed off his new-born baby Prince and pledged "I want my son to live a normal life."
"I'm in bliss 24 hours a day," one of the world's most famous rock stars told OK! magazine as he tenderly cradled his light-skinned son in his arms.

"There were shouts of joy when the baby was born. I couldn't believe the miracle I had just witnessed. It was unbelievable," he told the magazine in an photo exclusive said to have cost OK! 2.5 million pounds ($4 million).
But the choice of name by Jackson, 38, and his 37-year-old wife Debbie Rowe had no link with fellow pop superstar Prince, who has in turn frequently changed his own name.
"His name is Prince Michael Junior. My grandfather and great-grandfather were both named Prince so we have carried on the tradition and now we have a third Prince in the family," Jackson said.
Rowe said Jackson was a model father who changed nappies, fed his five-week old son and sung to him.

Jackson, who as a child star was sheltered from the real world and never enjoyed a normal boyhood, said of his own son: "I have lived in a fishbowl all my life and I want my son to live a normal life."

The painfully shy Jackson, transformed into an electrifying exhibitionist in his spectacular stage shows, has always found it difficult to relate to adults and the reclusive Peter Pan figure revels in the company of children.

In 1993, a 13-year-old boy sued Jackson, charging the singer molested him. The lawsuit was settled out of court for a reported $15 million and Jackson, who denied any wrongdoing, was never charged with a crime.
Jackson was previously married to Lisa Marie Presley, daughter of rock 'n' roll legend Elvis Presley, for 20 months. He married Rowe less than a year after the divorce.
Jackson and Rowe have known each other for several years. They met when she worked as a nurse in the office of the singer's Beverly Hills dermatologist.
He has denied tabloid newspaper reports that Rowe had been artificially inseminated, that he paid her $500,000 to have his child and that he would pay her $1.24 million when the baby was born.
Rowe told OK!; "I have married and had a baby with the man I will always love and I am on top of the world."
But she confessed to being bruised by the publicity from British tabloids who have dubbed him "Wacko Jacko."
"The only time I feel sad is when I see quotes attributed to him that I never said or when I hear late-night comedians taking cheap shots at my husband when they are not true," she said.

"Don't believe 99 percent of the garbage you read or hear. I know that we will be under increasing public scrutiny and I don't look forward to that but I know that will always be a part of being married to Michael."
